title: Electrochemical and hot corrosion behaviour of annealed AlCoCrFeNi HEA coating over steel.

recollection.intervention: Application of annealed AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy (HEA) coating
recollection.structure: Annealed HEA coating with potential phase stabilization
recollection.mechanism: Improved corrosion resistance due to the formation of stable oxide layers and uniform elemental distribution
recollection.results: Enhanced electrochemical and hot corrosion resistance compared to uncoated steel substrate

score.note: The recollection only generically identifies applying and annealing an AlCoCrFeNi coating, without plasma spraying, coating thickness, annealing temperatures, or the selected 550 °C condition. Phase stabilization is vague and omits the specific BCC/FCC phases, grain refinement, and reduced voids. Stable protective oxide formation is a correct mechanism beyond the title, though uniform elemental distribution is nonspecific. No quantitative hardness, electrochemical, or hot-corrosion results are recalled.
